segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: I wonder if you could spare a few minutes to do a survey on transport. It won’t take long.

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Lovely. The survey is on behalf of the local council. They’d like to know about what transport you use and any suggestions for improvement. Can I start by asking you how you travelled to town today?

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: Sure. I came on the bus.

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Great. Now can I get a few details about yourself?

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Great. Thanks. And can I have your address?

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Oh, right. I know that area. It’s Bradfield, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Great. And could I ask what your job is? Are you a student?

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: I’ve actually just finished my training. I’m a hairdresser. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Oh, right. And one more question in this section. What is the reason for you coming into town today?

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: Actually it’s not for shopping today, which would be my normal reason, but to see the dentist. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Now in this last section I’d like you to give us some ideas about the facilities and arrangements in the city for getting to and from work, er, any suggestions you have for improvements.

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: Well, something I’ve thought about for some time is that when I do walk and I’m doing a later shift, I think the lighting should be better. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: And of course, I think it’s a real shame they’ve been cutting down on the number of footpaths. They should have more of those. Then people would walk more.

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: And, I don’t think there are enough trains. That’s why I don’t use them – you have to wait so long. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Thanks. And finally I’d like to ask your opinion on cycling. As you may know, there’s a drive in the city to get more people to cycle to work.

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: But we realise that there are things which the council, but also employers, might do to help encourage workers to cycle to work.

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: Yep. Well, I have thought about it and where I work there are no safe places to leave your bikes. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: And also, I’d have to cycle uphill and on a hot day I’d arrive at work pretty sweaty so I think I’d need a shower somewhere at work. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LUISA
segments.en: And I suppose the last thing is that I wouldn’t be all that confident about cycling on such busy roads. I think I’d like to see you offering training for that [[ ]] , you know. I’d feel a lot better about starting if that was the case.

segments.speaker: INTERVIEWER
segments.en: Well, that’s very helpful. Thank you very much for your time.
